borders.before: the lecturer introduces herself, the series, and the learning objectives for this lecture
borders.after: what cancer is fundamentally as a genetic disease and how microenvironments and evolution contribute
borders.caseForKeeping: Subtopic 1 is pure administrative framing and learning objectives, whereas subtopic 2 begins substantive subject teaching.
borders.caseForMoving: Subtopic 2 directly introduces biological concepts, so no earlier or later subtopic serves as framing.
borders.caseForRemoving: Combining introductory framing with substantive lecture content ignores the convention that framing opens the lecture as its own topic.

borders.before: epidemiological global variations and genetic vs environmental predisposing factors
borders.after: infectious agents and pathogens driving cancer, including H. pylori, EBV, and HPV
borders.caseForKeeping: Subtopic 7 pivots specifically to infectious causes/pathogens, starting the detailed exploration of specific carcinogen classes.
borders.caseForMoving: Subtopic 6 discusses broad geographic variations across countries, while subtopic 7 introduces pathogens explicitly.
borders.caseForRemoving: The general balance of genetics/luck vs environment in subtopics 2-6 is distinct from the detailed mechanistic look at pathogens starting in subtopic 7.

borders.before: Burkitt lymphoma etiology, geographic distribution, malaria link, and chromosomal translocation
borders.after: dietary carcinogens, aflatoxin metabolism into reactive epoxides, and subsequent chemical/physical mutagens
borders.caseForKeeping: Subtopics 7-8 focus on infectious agents (viruses/bacteria/parasites), while subtopic 9 transitions to dietary toxins, chemicals, and promotion mechanisms.
borders.caseForMoving: Subtopic 8 concludes the Burkitt lymphoma case study; subtopic 9 clearly starts chemical/dietary mutagens.
borders.caseForRemoving: Infectious pathogenesis is distinct from chemical mutagenesis and tumor promotion via biochemical adducts/receptors.

borders.before: summary of mutagenic mechanisms, promoters, xenobiotic metabolism, and developmental susceptibility
borders.after: mutational signatures, DNA sequencing patterns, and methodologies to prove carcinogenicity
borders.caseForKeeping: Subtopic 17 is a clear summary of how agents damage DNA/promote tumors, while subtopic 18 shifts to the scientific methodology of identifying and proving carcinogens.
borders.caseForMoving: Subtopic 17 summarizes the previous section; subtopic 18 opens the methodology question ('How can we work out what's causing cancer?').
borders.caseForRemoving: The biological mechanisms of carcinogenesis (chemical/physical/promoters) are conceptually separate from the investigatory/testing methods used to detect them.

borders.before: the Ames test and in vitro toxicology assays
borders.after: wrap-up, risk-benefit assessment in everyday life, and lecture summary with concluding applause
borders.caseForKeeping: Subtopic 22 is the concluding closing section summarizing the lecture and offering final thoughts on risk/benefit.
borders.caseForMoving: Subtopic 21 finishes testing methods (Ames test); subtopic 22 begins 'So ultimately, it's all about the risks versus the benefits... So we will end it there with this summary'.
borders.caseForRemoving: Concluding lecture framing belongs in its own concluding topic.

insides.caseForDividing: Subtopics 2-3 explore intrinsic cellular biology and the conceptual roulette wheel, while 4-6 review known environmental exposures and epidemiological studies.
insides.caseForKeepingWhole: Subtopics 2-6 form a cohesive overview examining whether cancer is driven by intrinsic bad luck/genetics versus environmental exposure.

insides.caseForDividing: Subtopic 7 introduces various oncogenic pathogens broadly, while subtopic 8 is an in-depth case study of Burkitt lymphoma.
insides.caseForKeepingWhole: Both subtopics address infectious causes of cancer, with subtopic 8 acting as the prime exemplar of the concepts introduced in subtopic 7.

insides.caseForDividing: Subtopics 9-13 focus on chemical mutagens, UV radiation, and DNA adduct formation, while subtopics 14-17 focus on tumor promotion, inflammation, and host tissue susceptibility.
insides.caseForKeepingWhole: All subtopics from 9 to 17 systematically work through non-infectious environmental mechanisms of oncogenesis, concluding with a recap in 17.

insides.caseForDividing: Subtopic 18 covers molecular mutational signatures, whereas 19-21 cover epidemiological and experimental toxicology assays.
insides.caseForKeepingWhole: Subtopics 18-21 address the overarching question of how carcinogenicity is detected and proven across sequencing, epidemiology, animal models, and in vitro tests.

topics.label: Introduction and Course Overview
topics.groupedBecause: Introduces the lecturer, the structure of the cancer lecture series, and the key learning objectives for the session.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Intrinsic Risk versus Environmental Factors
topics.groupedBecause: Explores the fundamental drivers of cancer development, comparing intrinsic genetic mutations and endogenous cellular errors with environmental exposures and epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Pathogens and Infectious Causes of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: Examines how infectious agents drive oncogenesis, focusing on the epidemiological and molecular mechanisms demonstrated by Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical Mutagens, Promoters, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: Details how chemical carcinogens and radiation damage DNA through direct adducts, metabolic activation, tumor promotion, and developmental stage susceptibility.

topics.label: Methods for Determining and Validating Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: Describes the genomic, epidemiological, animal, and in vitro experimental strategies used to detect and evaluate carcinogenic exposures.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Assessment
topics.groupedBecause: Summarizes the lecture's core themes regarding environmental cancer risk and balances carcinogenic hazards against practical everyday choices.
